MIT's staff biography lists this earlier employment immediately before Alexander's NBER research position.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Geroid T. Robinson is the Columbia historian who became chief of the OSS R&A USSR Division.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name and initial, P-8 index grade, Columbia chronology, and named OSS division leadership align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Columbia's finding aid places his teaching before and through the period in which it identifies his wartime OSS role.
claims.match_notes: The name and role combination is highly distinctive; the physical Box 651 file remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Robinson taught in Columbia University's History Department from the 1920s onward before leading the OSS R&A USSR Division.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Columbia's finding aid directly pairs his long-running History Department teaching with his wartime OSS division chief role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the distinctive full name and institutional role match the index entry.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded and treated as the best-supported immediate and last civilian pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The source does not give a precise OSS appointment date, so the chronology is not labeled explicit immediate.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Barrington Moore is the Yale-trained sociologist who served as an OSS strategic analyst.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, P-5 index grade, Yale training, and Harvard's explicit OSS analyst description align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional obituary places Yale graduate study before wartime OSS service but does not state the exact transition date.
claims.match_notes: The physical Box 534 personnel file remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Moore pursued doctoral study in sociology at Yale before his wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard's institutional obituary identifies his Yale sociology doctorate and then his wartime OSS analyst service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar affiliation; immediacy is not established.
claims.match_notes: Student status is not converted into Yale employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Calvin B. Hoover is the Duke economist who served with the OSS R&A Branch from 1941 to 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and initial, Duke career, and CIA Historical Staff chronology align with the Box 347 index entry.
claims.temporal_assessment: The CIA history explicitly dates OSS service to 1941-1944.
claims.match_notes: The index supplies no grade, so no military or civilian grade is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Hoover held a continuing economics faculty appointment at Duke University before beginning OSS service in 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The archival-derived Duke biography and CIA history both place his Duke professorship well before his 1941-1944 OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded and treated as the best-supported immediate and last civilian pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: Sources differ slightly on whether the Duke appointment began in 1925 or 1927; that discrepancy is disclosed and does not affect the pre-OSS relationship.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Chandler Morse is the Federal Reserve economist who became an OSS R&A leader.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, P-8 index grade, official 1941 transition, and 1944 OSS branch order align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Official records directly bridge his Federal Reserve work and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The physical Box 540 personnel file remains unreviewed, but the official chronology is explicit.

claims.claim_text: Morse left the Federal Reserve Board's Division of Research and Statistics in 1941 to join OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Board's 1945 annual report explicitly describes the 1941 departure for OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by distinctive name and official transition record.
claims.match_notes: The Board assignment is not mislabeled as a civilian private-sector employer.

claims.claim_text: Before his Board assignment, Morse worked in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's Foreign Information Division.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Contemporary Board minutes document his 1935 transfer from the New York Reserve Bank to the Board.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by distinctive name and continuous official employment chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented earlier prewar employment and last identified civilian employer before the intervening Board assignment.
claims.match_notes: The Federal Reserve Bank and Board remain distinct organizations and relationship types.

claims.claim_text: The indexed First Lieutenant Sidney S. Alexander is the Harvard- and NBER-trained economist whose MIT biography dates OSS service to 1942-1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, commissioned rank, NBER chronology, and institutional OSS dates align.
claims.temporal_assessment: MIT's chronology places NBER research immediately before OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The physical Box 9 personnel file remains unreviewed; the full service number is not published.

claims.claim_text: Alexander conducted research for the National Bureau of Economic Research from 1940 to 1942 immediately before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: MIT supplies the consecutive 1940-1942 NBER and 1942-1945 OSS chronology; NBER confirms he remained on its payroll in early 1942.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded immediate affiliation and last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The sources support employment rather than merely professional affiliation.

claims.claim_text: While on NBER's payroll in early 1942, Alexander served as a part-time consultant to the Office of Price Administration.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NBER's contemporary annual report identifies both the payroll relationship and the OPA consulting assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate government assignment; the exact transition date to OSS is not stated.
claims.match_notes: OPA consulting is kept separate from NBER employment.

claims.claim_text: Alexander was a Harvard College Teaching Fellow in 1939-1940 before joining NBER.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: MIT's contemporary staff biography supplies the consecutive Harvard and NBER employment chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented earlier prewar employment, not the immediate pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The earlier Harvard role is kept out of the immediate-employer field.

research_attempts.query_text: "Geroid T Robinson" OSS Columbia employer; NARA, CIA Reading Room, university, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and general Russian-studies summaries were discovery-only; postwar Russian Institute leadership was excluded from the pre-OSS employer field.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified continuing Columbia History Department employment and OSS USSR Division leadership. CIA Reading Room exact-name searching produced no better pre-OSS employer source.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 651 for appointment paperwork and the exact Columbia-to-OSS transition date.

research_attempts.query_text: "Barrington Moore" OSS employer Yale; NARA, CIA Reading Room, Harvard, university, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and generic biographies were discovery-only; CIA hits concerned postwar publications or unrelated Congressional material and did not establish pre-OSS employment.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified Yale doctoral study and OSS analyst service. No reliable pre-OSS employer was established after the full protocol.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 534 for employment immediately before OSS and for the exact Yale-to-OSS chronology.

research_attempts.query_text: "Calvin B Hoover" OSS Duke employer 1941; NARA, CIA Reading Room, Duke archives, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia was discovery-only; direct Duke finding-aid access was blocked by a bot challenge, so the SNAC authority record derived from that finding aid was used and the access limitation recorded.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified Duke employment continuing into the 1941 OSS transition. Preserved the 1925/1927 start-year discrepancy and did not infer a personnel grade.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 347 for grade, appointment status, and whether the Duke appointment formally continued during OSS service.

research_attempts.query_text: "Chandler Morse" OSS Federal Reserve employer 1941; NARA, CIA Reading Room, FRASER, university, scholarly, newspaper, obituary, and archival-source review
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and unsourced summaries were discovery-only; postwar Cornell employment was excluded from pre-OSS claims.
research_attempts.research_notes: Official Federal Reserve records explicitly establish the 1935 New York Fed-to-Board transfer and 1941 Board-to-OSS transition; a CIA branch order corroborates his OSS identity.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 540 for the precise OSS appointment date and employment terms.

research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and commercial biographies were discovery-only; an official document with an inconsistent rank reference was not used for the employment claims and requires personnel-file context.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified Harvard employment, consecutive NBER-to-OSS chronology, and concurrent 1942 OPA consulting. The full service number remains private.
